designs.why: Clear one-ink hierarchy: bold lowercase 'the end' sits on the horizon, the half sun with cut stripes balances it, and the sailboat and gulls give a clean, readable linocut story at 3 m. Wave lines widen toward the bottom and the glitter column leads the eye well. The main production risk is the dense hairline sea just under the horizon, where the thin lines and tight gaps may fill in on a mesh screen and read as a grey mass or a blob. The thin boat wake squiggle and the stray dash at far right near y=1150 are also fragile.
designs.fix: Open up the top 15-20 sea lines: make strokes at least 0.5 mm thick with gaps of at least 0.6 mm, and drop every other line near the horizon. Thicken the boat wake squiggle and delete the stray dash at the right edge.
